overview:
This check monitors [Fly.io][1] metrics through the Datadog Agent.

**Minimum Agent version:** 7.57.0

[1]: https://fly.io/
setup:
Follow the instructions below to install and configure this check for an Agent running on a Fly application.

### Installation

The Fly.io check is included in the [Datadog Agent][2] package. We recommend deploying one Fly.io application dedicated to running the Datadog Agent. This agent can run the Fly.io check, which collects [Prometheus metrics][19] as well as some additional data from the [Machines API][20]. Additionally, you can configure the Agent to receive [traces](#Application-Traces) and custom metrics from all of your Fly.io applications inside the organization.

#### Deploying the Agent as a Fly.io application

1. Create a new application in Fly.io with the image set as the [Datadog Agent][15] when launching, or provide the image in the `fly.toml` file:

    ```
    [build]
        image = 'registry.datadoghq.com/agent:7'
    ```

2. Set a [secret][17] for your Datadog API key called `DD_API_KEY`, and optionally your [site][14] as `DD_SITE`.

3. Create a [read-only][23] authentication token.

4. In your app's directory, create a `conf.yaml` file for the Fly.io integration, [configure](#configuration) the integration, and mount it in the Agent's `conf.d/fly_io.d/` directory as `conf.yaml`:

    ```
    instances:
    - empty_default_hostname: true
      headers:
          Authorization: FlyV1 <YOUR_FLY_TOKEN>
      machines_api_endpoint: http://_api.internal:4280
      org_slug: <YOUR_ORG_SLUG>
    ```

5. [Deploy][16] your app.

**Note**: To collect traces and custom metrics from your applications, see [Application traces](#Application-traces).

### Configuration

1. Edit the `fly_io.d/conf.yaml` file, located in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your Agent's configuration directory, to start collecting your Fly.io performance data. See the [sample fly_io.d/conf.yaml][4] for all available configuration options.

2. [Restart the Agent][5].

### Validation

[Run the Agent's status subcommand][6] and look for `fly_io` under the Checks section.

metrics.name: fly_io.app.count
metrics.description: Count of apps

metrics.name: fly_io.instance.cpu.count
metrics.description: The amount of time each CPU (cpu_id) has spent performing different kinds of work (mode) in centiseconds

metrics.name: fly_io.instance.disk.io_in_progress
metrics.description: Incremented as requests are given to appropriate struct request_queue and decremented as they finish.

metrics.name: fly_io.instance.disk.reads_completed.count
metrics.description: This is the total number of reads completed successfully.

metrics.name: fly_io.instance.disk.reads_merged.count
metrics.description: Reads and writes which are adjacent to each other may be merged for efficiency. This field lets you know how often this was done.

metrics.name: fly_io.instance.disk.sectors_read.count
metrics.description: This is the total number of sectors read successfully.

metrics.name: fly_io.instance.disk.sectors_written.count
metrics.description: This is the total number of sectors written successfully.

metrics.name: fly_io.instance.disk.time_io.count
metrics.description: Counts jiffies when at least one request was started or completed. If request runs more than 2 jiffies then some I/O time might be not accounted in case of concurrent requests.

metrics.name: fly_io.instance.disk.time_io_weighted.count
metrics.description: Incremented at each I/O start, I/O completion, I/O merge, or read of these stats by the number of I/Os in progress (field 9) times the number of milliseconds spent doing I/O since the last update of this field.

metrics.name: fly_io.instance.disk.time_reading.count
metrics.description: This is the total number of milliseconds spent by all reads.

metrics.name: fly_io.instance.disk.time_writing.count

metrics.name: fly_io.instance.disk.writes_merged.count

monitors.title: Fly.io App Suspended
monitors.description: A Fly.io app can be suspended if the app exits or if the app does not have any traffic. This monitor tracks whether an app status is suspended for the last 10 minutes.
